relation.rationale: The near-critical expansion bound uses the quenched lower bound on p_c(C).

from_statement_quote: Let G be a countable undirected graph of maximum degree Delta>=2 with 0<p_c(G)<1. For each fixed p in (p_c(G),1], almost surely every infinite Bernoulli-p open component C and every o in C satisfy h(C,o)<=log(Delta^2+1)/log(p/(p-p_c(G))), where h(C,o)=inf{|boundary_E K|/|K|:K finite connected in C and o in K}. At p=p_c(G), almost surely all such h(C,o) equal zero. No simultaneity for uncountably many p is asserted.
to_statement_quote: Let G be a countable undirected graph, p_c(G)=inf{r:P_r(some infinite open component exists)>0}, and p in (0,1]. Almost surely every infinite open component C in independent Bernoulli-p bond percolation satisfies p_c(C)>=min{1,p_c(G)/p}. In particular, when p=p_c(G)>0, every such component has p_c(C)=1.

to_statement_quote: Let C be an infinite connected countable graph of maximum degree Delta>=2, o a vertex, and h=inf{|boundary_E K|/|K|:K finite connected and o in K}>0. Under independent Bernoulli-q bond percolation, if a=(1-q)^h<1/(Delta^2+1), then P_q^C(o belongs to an infinite open cluster)>=1-a/(1-Delta^2*a)>0. Consequently p_c(C)<=1-(Delta^2+1)^(-1/h).

relation.rationale: The decorated ray has exponential growth and degree 3 but p_c=1, contradicting the proposed growth-only implication.

from_statement_quote: There is an infinite connected graph H of maximum degree 3 with liminf_r|B_H(s_0,r)|^(1/r)>=sqrt(2)>1 and p_c(H)=1: attach a full finite binary tree of depth n by one edge to the nth vertex of a spine ray. It has infinitely many vertex orbits. Thus exponential volume growth and bounded degree alone do not imply p_c<1; quasi-transitivity cannot be dropped from that implication.
to_statement_quote: REFUTED CANDIDATE, not an accepted theorem: the proposed implication that every infinite connected bounded-degree graph of exponential volume growth has p_c<1. The decorated-ray counterexample disproves this implication. Checking the symmetry hypothesis on the ambient graph does not establish it for a random open cluster.

relation.rationale: The proposed injective bounded-distance branching network would force exponential ambient growth.

from_statement_quote: Let b>=2 and L>=1 be integers. If the rooted b-ary tree has an injective vertex map into a locally finite graph G with each parent-child image pair at distance at most L, then liminf_{r->infinity}|B_G(f(root),r)|^(1/r)>=b^(1/L)>1. Hence such a map cannot exist in a graph of subexponential volume growth.
to_statement_quote: REFUTED CANDIDATE, not an accepted theorem: the proposed construction of an injective b-ary tree with b>=2 and uniformly bounded parent-child graph distances inside a subexponential ambient graph. The branching-volume bound rules out this construction before any percolation probabilities are considered.
